clue.text: See 12
Stop shaving and take up female dress - outside line to Lincoln

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up lifts it from the bottom, so the word reads upward and backwards
the dress goes outside, wrapping round the following pieces like a garment round a body

blocks.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man
a row is a line of things
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname; 'to' attaches it to the line

explanation.surface: Someone gives up shaving and starts cross-dressing, apparently in tribute to the bearded Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Drag is women's clothes worn by a man. Lincoln's famous chin beard makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: If you stop shaving, hair on the chin and jaw keeps growing until you have whiskers.

clue.text: Argentinian girl has a row with Araucaria

blocks.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a tier is a row, as of seats
Araucaria is the setter, who calls himself I

explanation.surface: An Argentine girl is quarrelling with the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line here. Leopoldo Galtieri was the Argentine general who led the 1982 invasion of the Falklands.
explanation.definitionFit: General Galtieri headed Argentina's military junta, so he is an example of an Argentine person.

clue.text: Stunt, perhaps, during parade for motorists

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of parade, all of for and the start of motorists

explanation.surface: A stunt driver performs during a parade put on for motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunt' reads as a daredevil act, but it is the verb meaning to check growth; 'perhaps' warns that this is only one way to deform.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunting growth distorts the natural shape of something, one way of misshaping it.

clue.text: It's hell, chaps, do you hear? Pretend you're someone else

indicators.note: the question asks the solver to listen, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: Dis is the classical underworld, and guys are chaps

explanation.surface: Someone hails the lads with a complaint that life is hell, then urges them to play a role.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm, a crossword stand-in for hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To disguise yourself is to change your appearance so that people take you for another person.

clue.text: Long stop Craig coming in suffers at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept
one thing coming in goes inside another, here into the core letters

blocks.note: Ailsa Craig is a rocky island in the Firth of Clyde
the three central letters of suffers

explanation.surface: A cricketer called Craig fields at long stop, and the side suffers deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: A long stop in cricket is the fielder behind the wicketkeeper who stops balls he misses; Craig names the island Ailsa Craig.
explanation.definitionFit: A long stop is a last line of defence when the keeper fails, which is exactly what a backup safeguard provides.

clue.text: Like 17 and 22, an old boat for an airborne elite

definitions.note: 17 and 22 are US states, so this is another one

blocks.note: Noah's ark is the old boat
taken as written, placed after the boat
the Special Air Service, the British army's elite airborne regiment

explanation.surface: An old boat is fitted out for a crack air unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an old boat' is read as ARK followed by AN; the SAS is Britain's special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona and Colorado are American states, and so is Arkansas, the third member of the set.

clue.text: Like this little house in London?

definitions.text: Like this little house in London?

blocks.note: so means in this way
the short form of house

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tiny London house looks like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: Soho is a district of central London, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a lively district in London's West End, found in the capital as the clue hints.

clue.text: Angry that love is upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word is turned to read from the bottom

blocks.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Someone is cross that a lover is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as distressed, but in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore is an informal word for cross or resentful, as in being sore about losing.

clue.text: Part of body with bone on the same row

indicators.note: only a part of the word is wanted, the rest being dropped

blocks.note: the shin is the front of the leg, home of the shinbone
points back to the word body, so the other piece comes from it
the same word the clue opens with

explanation.surface: A body part with its bone lies on the same line.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Araucaria parse: the bone sits on a part of that same word, body, its tail. 'Row' is the noisy sort, rhyming with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindy is a noisy quarrel or uproar, the same as a row pronounced to rhyme with cow.

clue.text: Poke fun at beloved Parisian ornithologist

blocks.note: to twit is to tease or taunt
cher is French for dear or beloved

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a dear Parisian who studies birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A twitcher is British slang for a keen birdwatcher who travels to tick off rare species.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a dedicated birdwatcher, loosely a bird expert, which the clue calls a scientist of birds.

clue.text: Lease up, bank gets involved, as can't be told

indicators.note: things that get involved become entangled together, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lease expires and the bank intervenes in a way nobody may discuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspeakable is too bad or too great to be put into words, so it cannot be described.

clue.text: Forth's second, once first, with stock round in card-game

indicators.note: the cattle go round, surrounding the next letters

blocks.note: kine is an old plural of cow, livestock
taken as written
taken as written
bridge is the partnership card game

explanation.surface: The second crossing of the Forth once came first, along with a round of stock in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card-game' does double duty. The Forth is the Scottish firth near Edinburgh, and kine is an archaic plural of cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kincardine road bridge, opened in 1936, was the first road crossing low on the Forth and was later outranked by the Forth Road Bridge.

clue.text: Serious injury to love-child - love would shortly come into it

indicators.note: to come into something is to go inside it, so these letters are inserted

blocks.note: a by-blow is an old word for an illegitimate child
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
would is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A dire hurt done to an illegitimate child, made worse as love briefly arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: O + D goes after the first letter of BYBLOW. A by-blow is an archaic term for a child born outside marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is a heavy punch to the torso, and figuratively a severe setback or damaging shock.

clue.text: Panelling for cart that attracts tax

blocks.note: a wain is an old farm wagon
scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: Wooden panels are being bought for a cart that will incur duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are old words: the wain of Constable's painting The Hay Wain, and the scot that escaping it leaves you scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden lining fixed to the lower part of interior walls, a form of wall panelling.

clue.text: Second insult is incomplete, but you get the flavour

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: A second insult falls short, yet still leaves a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a spice from crocus stigmas, used to give dishes its distinctive taste and yellow colour.

clue.text: Old-fashioned in fashion in fashion business?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first piece is placed within the second

blocks.note: trad is short for traditional
the rage is the current craze

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether the dated look is back in style in the clothes world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' appears twice: first as wordplay, the rage, then as the clothes sense in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is the informal name for the clothing industry, the business of designing and selling garments.

clue.text: Touching 22 is the owner of Harry, some say  ...

indicators.note: how some people say it is how it sounds when spoken, dropped aitch and all

blocks.note: Harry with the h dropped, as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: Someone near Colorado is introduced as the person Harry belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 18 and 22: Arizona contains the Grand Canyon, which contains the Colorado river.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona and Colorado meet at the Four Corners, so the one state borders the other.

clue.text: ...  which contains the £1,000 container that ...

definitions.note: read on from 17: the feature that Arizona contains

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
a can is a container
yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: Part of a running sentence: a state holds a thousand-pound box that holds something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The three clues 17, 18 and 22 form one chain: each answer contains the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canyon is the great gorge in northern Arizona, so it is what that state holds.

clue.text: Covering for a wheel covering, so to speak

indicators.note: speaking the words out loud gives the sound that matters here

blocks.note: tyre is the British spelling of tire

explanation.surface: A covering is wanted for a wheel's rubber casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is clothing, the garments that cover a person's body.

clue.text: No relation to shellfish: it's a trick

blocks.note: surface: a disclaimer, as if denying kinship with a seafood dish
setter's reading: the word looks like the opening of a fried prawn dish's name but is etymologically unconnected

explanation.surface: A notice insists that something has nothing to do with seafood and is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAM is the first four letters of SCAMPI, the Norway lobster dish, but the two words share no ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, a confidence trick.

clue.text: Distinctly not parts of Blue Peter?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun or verb, the definition an adverb phrase meaning not clearly

indicators.note: only parts of the words are used, so letters are dropped from each

blocks.note: the first word of the programme's name
the final letter of Peter

explanation.surface: A question about the bits of a children's TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running British children's TV programme. The pieces are the start of Blue and the end of Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen without sharp outlines, the opposite of being clearly distinguished.

clue.text: ...  contains a flower with a beetle on it

definitions.text: a flower with a beetle on it

blocks.clueFragment: a flower with a beetle on it
blocks.note: surface: a bloom with an insect crawling on its petals

blocks.clueFragment: a flower with a beetle on it
blocks.note: setter's reading: a flower is something that flows, a river, and this river shares its name with a notorious potato pest

explanation.surface: The chain ends with a blossom carrying a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, one that flows. The Colorado runs through the Grand Canyon, and the Colorado beetle ravages potato crops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado is a river, and the Colorado beetle is named after the same region, so the river carries a beetle's name.

clue.text: Typically leaning to the right

blocks.note: surface: someone with conventional conservative politics
setter's reading: in printing type, a style whose letters slope rightwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Typically' hides 'in type', and 'the right' is a direction, not a political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic is the sloping typeface style whose letters slant towards the right.

clue.text: Master ingesting a toxic gas had the hand of God to help him

definitions.text: had the hand of God to help him

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the following pieces go inside

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
taken as written
radon is a radioactive gas

explanation.surface: An expert swallows poison gas, then gets divine help.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona scored with his hand against England in 1986 and said it was the hand of God.

clue.text: Hot stuff here? Cold stuff covers the West

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps round it, so one piece goes outside

blocks.note: frost is frozen dew
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A weather contrast: heat in one place while frost blankets the western regions.
explanation.walkthrough: Frowst is a British word for the warm, stale air of a closed room.
explanation.definitionFit: A frowst is a hot, stuffy, fuggy atmosphere, the sort found in a stale overheated room.
